Chinese

Greetings Divers!
Today it's Midsummer Eve here in Sweden and to celebrate we wanted to release a new patch, 1.04!

The focus for this patch has been adding ways for players to tailor their Heavy Metal Death Can experience in multiple ways. We've added difficulty modes for players who want a less unforgiving experience as well as those of you who are looking for a real challenge. These are chosen upon starting a new game but can be changed at any time in the options menu.

We've also added a lot of bonus options that are unlocked upon beating the game once. These include cheats to play around with but most importantly two Item Randomizing modes! One mode excludes key-items making a run more predictable in terms of progression, the other one is full random and that is just all kinds of chaos. Note that while we've tested it a fair bit full-random is still kind of experimental, there might be dragons!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614058/e51aad23711461843c80f8da992aca71698915e3.png"]

For the Speedrunners we've added an In-Game timer that pauses on room switching in order to be hardware agnostic. This is accessible from the Game Options Menu. Any additional features Speedrunners would like let us know!
Many players asked for an RE-Style Run+Down 180 degree turn and we have obliged, it's now in the game!
Added Difficulty options, Easy, Normal and Hard.
Added In-Game Timer option
RE-style Run+down 180 degree spin.
Added bonus content!
Two modes of Item randomization, Non-Key items and Full Random
Added Golden KLAS Cheat
Added Golden Pistol Cheat
Added Invulnerable Cheat
Added a new secret room, accessible after beating the game once
Additional fixes and tweaks
We're still looking into localization, announcement regarding that coming soon. Additional focus going forward is platform support and soundtrack!
Thanks to everyone who has stuck around and supported the game! This update is for the community and we hope you enjoy these new features!
Happy Midsummer!
Cheers!
/Toby

Greetings Divers!
Patch 1.02 has been deployed!

With patch 1.01 we feel the general experience of exploring the HMS Domherren is pretty solid balancing-wise. Wherever you go throughout your adventure you’re likely to find something useful. However, the bosses lacked some of that polish. We had focused on making the intended way of beating them work well that we neglected some of the more basic UX of the fight making them obtuse and frustrating.

With this patch we’ve addressed this, making sure that the bosses are legible and that they offer sufficient feedback. They’re still challenging but they’re way tighter and the player will have more opportunity to respond and participate. You can now also skip dialogues making replays and retrying the bosses less tedious.

Some players are having issues with resources being too scarce. We addressed this by having the Armorer sometimes handing out freebies depending on your inventory status. This was probably missed by everyone, not least the ones who may have needed it. Now he can give you a call on the phones scattered across the sub and tell you when there’s a freebie to be had.

items.text: Greetings Divers!

Heavy Metal Death Can has been out for almost a week and it's been a pleasure and a privilege to see the community embracing our little horror game. It is the studio's maiden voyage and it's been both heartwarming and harrowing watching streams and reading reviews of the game.

We're a small team with limited bandwidth and the amount of feedback we've gotten this week has been incredible. It gives us a clear picture of the state of the game and what works and what doesn't for our players.

We set out to make a game that was tough but fair, tuned so that players returning to the genre would feel adequately challenged, but we also wanted there to be an in for newer players by teaching them how these games are played. There are systems in place to make sure that players don't get left behind but they're too subtle and need tweaking.

The bosses are also in need of tweaking. We wanted them to be challenging, spikes of difficulty to make for rewarding wins and shake up the gameplay loop. It was never our intention for them to be unfair and after watching players struggle with them we've identified key issues which we'll adress specifically, especially on the first and last boss. These fixes will make the fights feel better and more fair while retaining their essence and their purpose as a memorable set piece fight.
We aim to release a patch on Friday with these fixes and we hope you'll give it a spin!

Thank you so much for being early adopters of our game. It's our debut title and the trust you put in us to deliver a solid game on day one is not lost on us. Thank you for being part of Heavy Metal Death Can!
Cheers!
/Toby
Greetings Divers!

Many thanks to everybody who got onboard the HMS Domherren yesterday for its maiden voyage! At the Krufs Productions HQ we've been monitoring our comms as well as player streams and put together a small patch that addresses some of the issues people have reported on the game.
Fixed collision that player could get stuck on.
Tweaks and balancing to first boss.
Fixed bug causing second boss to sometimes get stuck.
Minor visual fixes, improve visual clarity in some key places.
Fixed certain zombie attacks causing player to get stuck.
Fixed navigation bug in load-game menu.
And additional bug fixes

We're so happy and overwhelmed by the reception on the game, it means the world to us that the game, it's aesthetics and its characters is resonating with players and we want to make sure that you get the best Death Can experience possible!
Hope you have a lovely weekend and we invite you to hop aboard the HMS Domherren, we guarantee it will be a terrifying experience!
Cheers!
/Toby
Hope all is well!
At Krufs Productions HQ we're keeping busy with the alpha, just wrapping up the first draft of the final boss of the game but since we just hit this milestone I thought an update would be fitting!

Since last update we've put out a collection of short form making-of videos where I'm talking about art, audio and music production. I plan to make a couple more if I find the time, so any suggestions of something game dev related that you would want to see lemme know!
Here's a link to a playlist with these videos: [dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLOYVTzTkrlfx28uZTiiUZ1uYtZPR_0Ejd"]
This summer I had the pleasure to be invited to the La Boveda Podcast to talk about the game and Survival Horror in general:

One thing I mentioned in this interview is my view on melee weapons in Survival Horror and that we won't have any. Well, I'm happy to announce that we've backpedaled on that and have now developed a melee weapon that we feel works great within our design! I'll go into details on it in an upcoming dev short but for now we think this is a fresh implementation that doesn't take away from the resource management aspect of the game. And, it's really fun to use too! [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614058/2f75084161a00ac12590c119518c34e681be59b4.png"]Thank you so much for wishlisting our little horror game and for coming along on this journey! As we approach beta we'll have a lot of exciting updates coming your way but for now we wish you a happy horror season!
All the best, skål!
/Toby
